results.name: same_decade_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets in the same decade (same tens digit, 1-100 with 100 in its own decade) as at least one example minus yes rate for targets in a decade containing no example; observed > null means people use decade/tens-digit similarity more than the model, observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: same_decade_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets in the same decade (same tens digit, 1-100 with 100 in its own decade) as at least one example minus yes rate for targets in a decade containing no example; observed > null means people use decade/tens-digit similarity more than the model, observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    vals = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    is_ex = np.any(vals == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dec = np.floor(vals / 10)
    same = np.any(dec == np.floor(t / 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    a = same & ~is_ex
    b = ~same & ~is_ex
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: unanimity_rate
results.description: Fraction of distinct (set, target, trial_index) items whose repeated responses are all identical (all yes or all no), among items answered 2+ times; observed > null means people agree more (model's predicted probabilities are too intermediate/uncertain), observed < null means the model is too deterministic.

results.name: even_set_odd_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for odd targets after sets whose examples are all even (2+ examples); observed > null means the model over-commits to parity/even rules and people accept parity-violating numbers more, observed < null means people respect parity more strictly than the model.
results.code:
# name: even_set_odd_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for odd targets after sets whose examples are all even (2+ examples); observed > null means the model over-commits to parity/even rules and people accept parity-violating numbers more, observed < null means people respect parity more strictly than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True)
    n_ex = (s.str.count(",") + 1).values
    all_even = np.ones(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for c in ex.columns:
        col = ex[c]
        v = col.fillna("0").astype(int).values
        all_even &= (col.isna().values) | (v % 2 == 0)
    m = all_even & (n_ex >= 2) & (t % 2 == 1)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[m].mean())

results.name: near_example_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets within distance 2 of the nearest example number (all sets); observed > null means people show more local numeric-similarity generalization than the model, observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: near_example_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets within distance 2 of the nearest example number (all sets); observed > null means people show more local numeric-similarity generalization than the model, observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    vals = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(vals - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    m = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 2)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[m].mean())

results.name: shared_digit_effect
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets containing a digit that appears in every example minus yes rate for non-example targets containing none of the examples' digits (multi-example sets with a common digit); observed > null means people generalize by shared digits more than the model, observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: shared_digit_effect
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets containing a digit that appears in every example minus yes rate for non-example targets containing none of the examples' digits (multi-example sets with a common digit); observed > null means people generalize by shared digits more than the model, observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True)
    n_ex = s.str.count(",") + 1
    ts = t.astype(str)
    common = np.ones(len(df), dtype=bool)
    tgt_common = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    tgt_any = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    has_common = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    is_ex = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for c in ex.columns:
        is_ex |= (ex[c].fillna("-1").astype(int) == t).values
    for d in "0123456789":
        in_all = np.ones(len(df), dtype=bool)
        in_any = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
        for c in ex.columns:
            col = ex[c]
            present = col.notna().values
            contains = col.fillna("").str.contains(d).values
            in_all &= (~present) | contains
            in_any |= contains
        td = ts.str.contains(d).values
        has_common |= in_all
        tgt_common |= in_all & td
        tgt_any |= in_any & td
    base = (n_ex.values >= 2) & has_common & ~is_ex
    a = base & tgt_common
    b = base & ~tgt_any
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: inside_range_mismatch_parity
results.description: Among 2+ example sets, yes rate for targets strictly inside the examples' [min,max] span that share NO common structure with the examples (parity differs from a parity-uniform set or set is mixed-parity) minus the same for outside-span targets; observed > null means people use a magnitude/interval region beyond what rule-based concepts allow and the model under-produces it.
results.code:
# name: inside_range_mismatch_parity
# description: Among 2+ example sets, yes rate for targets strictly inside the examples' [min,max] span that share NO common structure with the examples (parity differs from a parity-uniform set or set is mixed-parity) minus the same for outside-span targets; observed > null means people use a magnitude/interval region beyond what rule-based concepts allow and the model under-produces it.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True)
    n_ex = (s.str.count(",") + 1).values
    vals = ex.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    lo = np.nanmin(vals, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(vals, axis=1)
    par = np.where(np.isnan(vals), np.nan, vals % 2)
    pmin = np.nanmin(par, axis=1); pmax = np.nanmax(par, axis=1)
    uniform = pmin == pmax
    mismatch = (~uniform) | (t % 2 != pmin)
    is_ex = np.any(vals == t[:, None], axis=1)
    base = (n_ex >= 2) & mismatch & ~is_ex
    a = base & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    b = base & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: n_examples_slope
results.description: Yes rate on 1-example sets minus yes rate on 4-example sets (non-example targets); observed > null means people's generalization narrows with more examples more than the model's (or the model is too broad for single examples), observed < null means the model narrows too much.
results.code:
# name: n_examples_slope
# description: Yes rate on 1-example sets minus yes rate on 4-example sets (non-example targets); observed > null means people's generalization narrows with more examples more than the model's (or the model is too broad for single examples), observed < null means the model narrows too much.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n_ex = (s.str.count(",") + 1).values
    vals = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    is_ex = np.any(vals == t[:, None], axis=1)
    a = (n_ex == 1) & ~is_ex
    b = (n_ex == 4) & ~is_ex
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: set_yes_rate_dispersion
results.description: Standard deviation across number sets (with 10+ responses) of the per-set yes rate; observed > null means people's overall willingness to generalize varies across sets more than the model predicts (some sets drawing near-total rejection, others broad acceptance), observed < null means less.
